name: St. Joseph Basilica
history: Polish immigrants who came to Webster after the failed January Insurrection of 1863 founded St. Joseph in 1887, the first Polish parish in New England. The parishioners laid the foundations of the wooden first church themselves. Under Msgr. Anthony Cyran the present church was completed by 1914. After a major renovation it was rededicated in 1997, and John Paul II named it a basilica in 1998.
arch: Gothic Revival in brick by John W. Donohue, longtime architect of the Diocese of Springfield, with twin towers and spires.
features: A statue of Pope John Paul II on the front lawn was dedicated in 2011 for the parish's 125th year.
The parish school reached 1,090 pupils when its new building opened in 1924.

look.d: The towers rise over Webster's mill town streets.
The first church cost $2,700; parishioners taxed themselves two dollars a month to build it.

fun: By parish tradition, the site was chosen because moss on an old stone there grew in the shape of a cross.
journal: The oldest Polish parish in New England. Built by people who fined themselves for missing work days.
